subject.title: Proposal: safer self-update with pre-update backup + health check + auto-rollback/restore

question: Should OpenClaw core own an integrated opt-in safe-update transaction that snapshots state, runs real post-update checks, and restores or rolls back on failure?
rationale: The remaining work is not a narrow bug fix: it defines updater product scope, secret handling, restore semantics, retention policy, and live smoke-check criteria across core state and plugins.

options.title: Sponsor a scoped core safe-update design
options.body: Define a default-off core updater mode and split implementation into reviewed pieces for snapshots, retention, health/smoke checks, and restore/rollback policy.

options.title: Split into narrower canonical issues
options.body: Use the open backup/restore, scanner, auto-update, and external-updater items as the only implementation tracks and leave this issue as an umbrella reference.

options.title: Keep this outside core for now
options.body: Document the community auto-update kit and manual recovery flow while declining automatic restore/rollback until the updater architecture changes.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a scoped core safe-update design
recommendation.body: Define a default-off core updater mode and split implementation into reviewed pieces for snapshots, retention, health/smoke checks, and restore/rollback policy.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the current keep-open product review and is tied by history to the inspected update and backup surfaces.
